messages.subject: Re: Cardinal 1.3
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paco,

These features are still experimental. See "?readMSIData" in Cardinal 1.3 or later (from Github or Bioc-devel) for a description of some of the new arguments for attaching data without loading it. This is done via the "attach.only" argument. Using "attach.only=TRUE" will only load the metadata, and access spectra and images on-demand.

Currently, only a subset of features are supported for such datasets. Most important right now is whether your data is already pre-processed,  or if it will fit into memory after pre-processing. None of the statistical analysis methods will work with data-on-disk yet. However, most of the visualization and pre-processing steps will work. Currently, you will need to process the data down to a size that can fit into memory before any statistical analysis can be done. (I hope to have support for analysis on processed data larger-than-memory in subsequent versions, but it will not be ready for the next Bioconductor release next month.)

Right now, if you need to do normalization, smoothing, or baseline reduction prior to peak-picking or binning/resampling, the resultant dataset (which will be at least as big as the original raw data) will be put into memory. However, if you can skip straight to peak-picking or binning/resampling, then you have more options, since the resultant dataset will still be put into memory but it will be smaller than the original.

By April 15 at the latest (since that is the release date for Bioconductor 3.3), I will have a new version with a "batchProcess" method which will allow streamlining the pre-processing steps so that multiple processing steps can be performed before loading everything into memory. If you need to do other pre-processing prior to peak-picking, etc., on data-on-disk, this method will make that possible soon.

-Ky

messages.subject: Remove legend
messages.body_plain: Is there maybe a way to remove the legend of the images created when applying the plot or image functions?
messages.body_snippet: Is there maybe a way to remove the legend of the images created when applying the plot or image functions?

messages.subject: Re: Remove legend
messages.body_plain:
Use "key=FALSE" for removing the legends on superposed plots.
Use "strip=FALSE" for removing the strip labels.
Use "colorkey=FALSE" for removing the ion image color keys.

:-)

messages.subject: loading large datasets with Cardinal
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

we are trying to load large processed imzml files (120GB on disk)
our server with 130GB RAM does not make it

my questions are
- what is the expected size in RAM (processed imzml of 120GB) ?
- is there a way to convert it to the smaller continuous form on our server (130GB RAM) ?
- is there a way to split the data for loading into RAM ?

thank you !
:-) Uli

messages.subject: Re: loading large datasets with Cardinal
messages.body_plain:
Hi Uli,

It is difficult to tell the exact size of the final loaded dataset for 'processed' imzML files because it will depend on the bin size.

For 'processed' imzML, the data must be read completely, and reading the file will create an intermediate dataset at least as large as the .ibd file plus extra space for the metadata parsed from the .imzML file.

I'm sorry, but unlike for 'continuous' imzML, there is currently no way within Cardinal to split the data or process it down to a more manageable size for 'processed' imzML if the full dataset cannot be loaded into memory.

It is in our plans to be able to process this data-on-disk without loading all of it for 'processed' imzML like we can (to a limited extent) for 'continuous' imzML, but it will be several months before this can be added.

-Ky
